lead: he had seen the work before he saw you, and by the second handshake you knew which part of it he had already decided to use. you showed him the rest anyway.
sun: the work arrives in a room before you do, and it arrives finished — good enough that a stranger has an opinion about you assembled before you speak. none of it travels with terms attached. so first meetings begin somewhere in the middle: the person opposite has handled the thing, admired it, worked out what it would do for them, and comes to the table with that already settled.
moon: and you see it happen. the small greed in the first minute — the way he says the process rather than your process, the question about who else has been shown it — arrives complete while he is still being charming. nothing comes with the seeing, no lever, no exit, so it becomes storage: his face at that minute, entire, still legible to you eleven years on.
pull: you knew at the handshake. the knowing came with nothing to do, so he left with the work and you kept the minute he decided to have it, exact, ever since.
tension: you handed it over with both hands and never let go of the afternoon, and those two do not read as one person. he remembers a friendly meeting, because for him it was one. years later something in your voice tells him he is still being held to something, and he is right, and the evidence is a face he made at a table that neither of you can produce. unforgiving is the word people land on.
cost: a stranger is legible to you inside two minutes — what they came for, what they will do with it — and the reading holds up every time. nothing in you converts it into a smaller offer, so the work goes out to people you have correctly read as takers, and what accrues is a register of exact minutes, held against people who have forgotten the meeting.

lead: the work is yours and the room it sits in was furnished before you were born. visitors are shown both in one sentence, and by its end the good thing has become a feature of the institution.
sun: in a place where most of what gets produced belongs to nobody, one body of work is signed, and it is yours, and it is good enough that the institution puts it in front of visitors. you have never held a version of it in reserve, never attached a condition to its use, never been the person who says what can and cannot be done with it. it goes into the building complete.
moon: the position predates you by three occupants, and its first instruction is that you are not seen minding anything. the room reads that as consent and returns it as manners — a note after the fact, a line in the programme, thanks in the third paragraph. nobody here has been rude to you about your own work. nobody has asked either, and the two arrive as one courtesy.
pull: a chair you did not build, and inside it the one thing you did. it is handled by everyone, always beautifully, and the beauty of the handling is what makes it unanswerable.
tension: everything done to it arrives as a tribute — a feature, a reissue, a wing that will carry the name — and tributes have no refusal form. from your position, declining one lands as a compliment turned down in public, and gets read as vanity or as an old grievance nobody can locate. not precious about the work is the phrase used approvingly at your own table, by people who are naming a missing part.
cost: a place like this cannot generate work at that standard on its own, and you supply it without terms, which is why the building has grown around it. what happens to it next is settled elsewhere and arrives as an announcement — you and the newest person on the floor read the same circulated note about a thing with your name printed under it.

lead: they booked a room sized to the reputation, and what you carried into it was the object itself — narrow, finished, very good. one of those is a promise; the other can be inspected.
sun: the thing you make is good, and good things bring their own crowd — you have never had to arrange that part, and you have never put a frame around it. no preface, no scale-setting, no this is one narrow thing done properly. it goes out bare and it earns exactly what it is worth, from anyone who looks at it. what makes that a problem is everything else standing next to it.
moon: you arrive at a scale you did not set and cannot lower. before anyone opens the thing they have been told what it will be, at a volume that comes off you and not off the work — and the work then has to be that. the width also makes it look public: people use it, adapt it, teach it, without once experiencing that as taking.
pull: the impression is larger than the work and the work is better than the impression, and you cannot shrink one or argue for the other, so the good thing pays the difference.
tension: the correction, when it comes, gets passed on the object: overrated, by people adjusting an estimate the object never made. the width that set it was never a claim and cannot be withdrawn, and the only answer available is you giving a smaller account of your own work, which sounds like modesty and reads as confirmation. so the thing you did properly carries a debt run up by the room, and the closest readers arrive already braced.
cost: the work survives close inspection, which is rare in anyone this widely discussed, and whoever does inspect it comes away with something usable for years. no assessment of it reaches you clean, though. praise is sized to the room and doubt is sized to the room, and whether the object is as good as you think is the one question the width will not let anyone answer.

lead: you stopped nine years ago, completely, the way you stop things. the thing you made did not stop, and your name is still the first word on it, and letters still come addressed to a person who ended.
sun: what you made went out finished and it went out bare — no clause, no reversion, nothing held in the drawer for a bad year. so it is still working: in print, on walls, in other people's teaching, admired by people who were children when you did it. leaving removed you from the room and left the object standing exactly where it was, under your name.
moon: the ending was total — the appetite went, the skill went, the reasons went, and what is left cannot do the thing and has no wish to. the owing does not shed. a reissue wants a signature, a student wants the story, a hall wants you on a stage explaining a choice made by somebody whose mind you no longer have.
pull: you shed the whole of it and the name stayed on. what is done to that work now is decided in rooms you are not in, by people who assume someone is minding it.
tension: nobody accepts that it ended, because the evidence against you is out in public doing its job — the thing is admired this year, so the maker is treated as current. you get introduced in the present tense. the offer to come and do it again arrives every second spring, kindly, from people who would be hurt to hear that the person they are inviting was finished a decade ago. saying it plainly gets heard as fishing.
cost: you can finish a whole life in a season and carry none of it out, and the thing you made stands up without you, which most work does not. it is also alone. it gets cut, retitled, hung wrong, taught as an example of what you were arguing against, and the corrections are available only to a person who no longer exists.
